issues.legal_issue: The land-reform statute does not require a civil court to refer a tenancy question to a tribunal when a local authority sues for possession of its land after the lease has expired and the occupant is alleged to be in unauthorised occupation.
material_facts: The land belonged to a local authority and had been leased by it to the occupant for a fixed term.
The lease expired by efflux of time, and the occupant did not deliver possession.
The local authority sued for possession and damages for unauthorised occupation.
The occupant sought a stay and a reference to the tribunal, claiming to be a tenant or deemed tenant.
issues.conclusion: The statutory exception for land belonging to or held on lease from a local authority left only the provision concerning rent applicable. The suit was for possession and damages, not rent; after the lease expired, the occupant was in unauthorised occupation. No question could therefore be referred to the tribunal, and the civil suit was not barred from proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 107 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, only section 8 applies to land belonging to or held on lease from a local authority. Section 8 concerns rent and did not apply to a suit for possession and damages for unauthorised occupation. Sections 133 and 112(B)(b) did not provide for a tribunal reference in those circumstances, and the statutory definition of tenant did not revive a tenancy that had ended when the lease expired. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.local_authority_owned_land: The land belonged to a local authority.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired: The occupant's fixed-term lease from the local authority ended, and the occupant remained on the land.
predicates.civil_possession_suit_for_unauthorized_o: The local authority brought a civil suit seeking possession on the ground that the occupant remained without authority.

issues.definition: When a local authority seeks civil possession of its land from an occupant whose fixed-term lease has expired, a tribunal reference under the land-reform law is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant cannot obtain protection against eviction under a temporary tenant-protection enactment when the land falls outside its scope and the enactment is no longer in force.
material_facts: The occupant claimed protection under a temporary enactment that prohibited eviction.
The land was outside the scope of that enactment.
The enactment had ceased to be in force by the time the occupant sought to rely on it.
issues.conclusion: The occupant could not rely on the temporary enactment for protection against eviction, and the claimed protection did not warrant a tribunal reference.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the Mysore Tenants (Temporary Protection from Eviction) Act, 1961 did not apply to the land and had ceased to operate. It therefore afforded no protection against eviction in this case. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.temporary_eviction_protection_claim: The occupant claimed protection against eviction under a temporary tenant-protection enactment.
predicates.land_outside_protection_law_scope: The land was outside the scope of the enactment said to provide protection.
predicates.protection_law_no_longer_in_force: The enactment had ceased to be in force when the occupant sought to rely on it.

issues.definition: A temporary eviction-protection claim does not succeed if the land is outside the enactment's scope or the enactment is no longer in force.
